title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document provides a single-page reference for new and current Redwood employees covering: working at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and a practical guide to the internal tools you will use day-to-day. It is intended for broad consumption by engineering, product, and company teams.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

- Mission alignment: We prioritize predictable, economical inference. All teams should be able to succinctly connect their work to customer value.
- Core values: shipping responsibly, engineering-first, customer-centric reliability, and continuous improvement.
- Ways of working: asynchronous-first communication, documented design decisions (ADRs), weekly check-ins with managers, and quarterly goals (OKRs).

Onboarding expectations for managers and new hires:
1. Manager: assign a buddy in the first 24 hours, schedule a 30/60/90 plan review at week 1, 4, and 12.
2. New hire: complete identity, equipment, and security checklist within first 3 business days.

2) Roles and career ladders

- Role families covered here: Software Engineering, SRE, Applied ML / Research, Product Management, Design, Sales / Customer Success, People Ops, Finance.
- Leveling philosophy: We grade on impact, scope, autonomy, and mentorship. Each career ladder describes expectations for IC and manager tracks.

Representative leveling matrix (summary):
| Level | IC title (examples) | Scope & expectations | Typical years of experience |
|-------|---------------------|----------------------|----------------------------|
| L1    | Associate Engineer   | Task-level execution, close mentoring, clear ownership of small features | 0-2 |
| L2    | Engineer            | Feature ownership, debugging at service-level, collaborates cross-team | 2-4 |
| L3    | Senior Engineer     | Design and deliver medium systems, mentor L1-L2, influences roadmap | 4-7 |
| L4    | Staff Engineer      | Cross-service design, leads technical initiatives, strong mentoring | 7+ |
| L5    | Principal / Architect | Company-level technical strategy, large-scale system ownership, represents Redwood externally | 10+ |

Promotion process (high level):
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet with 3-5 examples of work mapped to ladder criteria.
2. Manager collects peer feedback and writes a review against the rubric.
3. Calibration committee reviews and approves, typically on a monthly cycle.
4. HR communicates outcome and updates compensation if approved.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Key benefits (high-level):
- Health: Medical/Dental/Vision plans with multiple tier options and employer contribution details.
- Time off: 20 PTO days + public holidays + flexible parental leave policy (primary: 18 weeks, secondary: 8 weeks) and caregiver leave.
- Financial: Competitive salaries, equity grants, 401(k) with employer match (US), pension guidance for EMEA.
- Learning & development: Annual training stipend ($2,000 USD), conference budget, internal mentorship program.
- Wellbeing: EAP, monthly wellness allowance, access to remote co-working stipends and ergonomic equipment budget.

How to request benefits changes or support:
1. Submit a benefits case via the HR portal (link in the tools section).
2. For urgent payroll or benefits errors, email payroll@redwood-inference.com and cc your People Ops partner.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring principles:
- Inclusive hiring: structured interview guides, job descriptions with clear success criteria, diverse interview panels.
- Candidate experience: timely communication, feedback within 7 business days after onsite, clear interview roadmap.

Interview process (standard engineering role):
1. Recruiter screen (30-45 min): role fit and motivation.
2. Technical screen (45-60 min): coding or systems discussion; sometimes take-home exercise.
3. Onsite loop (4-5 interviews, 3-4 hours): design, coding/debugging, system design, culture/leadership.
4. Debrief & hiring packet: interviewers submit feedback within 48 hours; hiring committee makes recommendation.
5. Offer & negotiation: People Ops handles offer details, background checks, and start-date coordination.

New hire 30/60/90 checklist (examples):
- Day 0-3: HR forms, equipment, access to Slack/GitHub/Jira, intro to buddy.
- Week 1: team orientation, codebase walkthrough, first small ticket assigned.
- Month 1: complete three training modules, demo first contribution.
- Month 3: performance check-in and finalize 90-day goals.

Offboarding checklist (summary):
- Revoke access (IT), return equipment, conduct exit interview, ensure knowledge handoff.

5) Internal tools guide (practical quick-reference)

Primary tools and common flows:
- Identity & Access: Okta (SSO). For new-app access requests use the Access Request form in the People Ops portal.
- Communication: Slack (channels: #all, #eng, #prod, #sre, #random). Use threads for focused discussions.
- Documentation: Confluence (this site) — search first, create pages under the correct space. Use templates: PRD, Runbook, ADR.
- Source control & CI: GitHub (org: redwood-inference), standard branch policy: feature/*, release/*, hotfix/*. CI: GitHub Actions with checks enforced by protected branches.
- Issue tracking & roadmaps: Jira. Use components and labels consistently. Create epics for cross-team work and link PRs to Jira issues.
- Deployments & infra: Deployment requests go through the internal deployment portal; production changes require an approved change request for high-impact services.
- Observability: Grafana dashboards (team-specific), Sentry for error grouping, Honeycomb for distributed traces. For urgent incidents open the on-call rotation in PagerDuty.
- HR & payroll: BambooHR / Workday (region dependent) — raise changes and time-off requests here.

Common CLI / Git patterns (examples):
- Clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/<repo>.git
- Create branch: git checkout -b feature/<short-description>
- PR template: include summary, testing steps, rollback notes, Jira ticket link.

6) Runbooks & incident basics

- All services must have a high-level runbook in Confluence with on-call contacts, common symptoms, mitigation steps, and escalation path.
- On-call rotations: 2-week primary, 4-week secondary. Define SLOs at the service level (example SLO: 99.9% success rate for /generate requests, p95 latency < 300ms).

7) Administrative & operational notes

- Expense policy: submit within 30 days with receipts. Approval chain: manager -> finance.
- Office & remote work policy: hybrid-first with team-determined core days and required quarterly in-person offsites for cross-functional planning.

Appendices

A. Quick reference contacts
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood-inference.com
- IT helpdesk: it-support@redwood-inference.com
- Security: security@redwood-inference.com

B. Templates and links (consolidated)
- New hire checklist template: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-checklist
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/promotion-packet-template
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbook-template

C. Table: Access levels and approvers
| Resource | Default access | Approver | Time to provision |
| Okta app: Confluence | all employees | People Ops | 1 business day |
| GitHub: org repos | engineering/product | Repo owner | same day |
| Production deployment access | senior eng or SRE | Team lead + Change Board | 1-2 business days |

If you have questions or need exceptions (confidential hires, legal constraints, or special onboarding for Private deployment customers), contact People Ops or your People Partner.

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (owner listed above).
- Review cadence: annual review and after significant policy changes (e.g., benefits or major tooling shifts).
- How to propose changes: open a pull request on the handbook repo with the proposed edits and include at least one reviewer from People Ops and one from Engineering.
summary: Comprehensive employee guide covering culture, role ladders, promotions, benefits, hiring and onboarding, and internal tooling quick references.
